incidents.victim: European grocery retailers, food processors, and blood services (France-led, 11+ countries)
incidents.vector: IRGC cyber unit Shahid Kaveh sabotaged internet-exposed refrigeration controllers and Schneider Electric industrial equipment, likely via default credentials or unpatched software, forcing units into defrost mode.
incidents.impact: Two attack waves (Oct. 11-12 and Nov. 1-2) spoiled food and caused at least 15 fires at roughly 700 French supermarkets before spreading to 11+ European countries, hitting blood-service sites and hydroelectric facilities. France formally attributed the campaign to Iran's IRGC and opened a criminal investigation, superseding earlier unverified hacktivist claims.

incidents.vector: Attacker exploited a flaw in Mittwald's Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, used to connect customer AI assistants to its mStudio hosting platform, to gain unauthorized access.
incidents.impact: 56 customer hosting projects were compromised; the intruder went undetected for eight days and reportedly moved through systems at AI-accelerated speed before being discovered and contained.

incidents.vector: Ransomware group BYOD compromised university systems and claimed data theft; the initial access method has not been disclosed.
incidents.impact: Campus devices and systems were impacted, prompting the university to tell students and staff to shut down devices and disconnect from campus WiFi; BYOD listed Vanderbilt on its leak site and claimed stolen data.

incidents.vector: Hackers gained unauthorized access to company files between Jan. 18 and Feb. 8, 2026; the initial access method was not disclosed.
incidents.impact: At least 85,804 Texas and 1,027 Vermont customers (plaintiffs' attorneys allege over 1.3 million total) had Social Security numbers, driver's licenses, medical records, health insurance data, and financial information stolen; no group has claimed credit.

incidents.vector: New ransomware and extortion group WhiteArmor claims to have breached Maersk's logistics platform; the initial access method was not disclosed.
incidents.impact: WhiteArmor claims to have stolen 10GB of data including driver records, staff accounts, and delivery receipts, and is demanding a $5 million Bitcoin payment; Maersk has not confirmed the incident.

incidents.vector: Belarusian opposition group Cyber Partisans and Ukrainian hacker operation Silent Crow obtained confidential internal data from Rosstat, Russia's statistics agency.
incidents.impact: Leaked records indicate Russia has recorded roughly 400,000 deaths of its soldiers fighting in Ukraine since the 2022 invasion, far above official public figures; the data was shared with Bloomberg News and other outlets.

incidents.victim: EU politicians, law enforcement officials, and journalists
incidents.vector: NoName057(16) published doxxed personal information on a dark web portal and offered cryptocurrency rewards for additional details about the targets and their families.
incidents.impact: 18 high-profile targets were exposed, including Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani, Eurojust's president, Europol's cybercrime chief, Germany's federal police president, and journalists covering Russian hacking; Tajani called it an intimidation campaign and G7 ministers discussed a joint response.

incidents.victim: Executive Office of the President (White House network)
incidents.vector: Staffer devices on the White House network were running residential-proxy apps (including Infatica) bundled in free software, letting commercial proxy services resell the network's IP addresses to paying customers.
incidents.impact: Security firms Layer3 Intel and Synthient found 28 separate residential-proxy services exiting through the White House's dedicated network over a month-long period, with 236 observed exit events, exposing a sensitive government network to anonymized third-party traffic of unknown origin.

incidents.victim: Android TV box and IoT device owners worldwide
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — ad fraud and proxyware monetization
incidents.vector: Chinese TV box manufacturer Videostrong Technology Co. pre-loaded malware onto devices, enrolling them in the XCPE botnet and installing residential-proxy and ad-fraud modules from affiliate services.
incidents.impact: More than 1.3 million Android TV set-top boxes, plus additional IoT devices such as telehealth equipment and karaoke machines, were secretly used to resell victims' internet connections and commit ad fraud; Google and partners severed the botnet's infrastructure, expected to cut off over 10 million additional compromised devices.

incidents.victim: Palo Alto Networks customers with internet-exposed PAN-OS management interfaces
incidents.vector: Attackers chained the critical PHP2Shell remote-code-execution flaws (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) with a Linux kernel privilege-escalation bug to gain root access to exposed PAN-OS management interfaces.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 confirmed active exploitation against the small fraction (about 0.02%) of its global installed base with internet-facing management interfaces; each affected customer was individually notified, and patched customers were unaffected. Researchers later judged the broader PHP2Shell threat largely fizzled relative to initial fears.

incidents.victim: Space/satellite, defense & aerospace, and policy-research organizations
incidents.vector: The actor exploited CVE-2026-20127, an authentication-bypass flaw in Cisco SD-WAN Catalyst Controllers, to gain unauthorized access and deploy the custom "KeyDrift" malware framework inside the control plane.
incidents.impact: KeyDrift intercepted decrypted SD-WAN control traffic and exfiltrated session metadata and data-plane encryption keys; researchers assessed the operator's infrastructure overlaps with a covert access network linked to Chinese state-sponsored activity targeting critical infrastructure.

incidents.victim: U.S. and allied businesses (DPRK remote IT worker scheme)
incidents.vector: DPRK IT workers used fraudulent documents, stolen identities, and fabricated personas, aided by AI tools, to secure remote employment with U.S. and allied companies, then used that access to deploy malware, exfiltrate data, and extort employers.
incidents.impact: Treasury sanctioned 10 individuals and one entity, facilitators and financial networks based in Russia and North Korea, tied to schemes that have generated hundreds of millions of dollars for DPRK weapons programs; the action follows related Australian and EU designations this month.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached Moldovan government networks and began extracting data before IT staff detected the exfiltration.
incidents.impact: The personal information of roughly one-third of Moldova's population was stolen; officials shut down 82 public digital services and 30 government networks to contain the breach and prevent further exfiltration.

incidents.victim: 40+ port authorities, maritime operators, and global shipping companies
incidents.vector: Ransomware and data-extortion group n0n breached CyberLogitec, a South Korean maritime IT platform provider, and used that access to pivot into the networks of its downstream customers.
incidents.impact: More than 40 port authorities, maritime, and global shipping companies, about half of them CyberLogitec customers, were listed on n0n's leak site following the supply-chain compromise; the group's payment deadline for victims expired Oct. 19.
